paras: Different textiles and other materials are worked with simple braiding techniques; mostly, thread into bands and surfaces. These are organized into textured surfaces with and without open spaces or through incorporating open spaces and branching the bands or threads, crossing-uniting, and again braiding into surfaces. The color selection is limited to one or two areas. In advanced exercises the students work with techniques requiring two and three braiding directions.
In the following two examples various types of threads are braided and formed into surfaces. Open spaces and branching bands allow crossing and penetration.
